prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Regional Dispatch Center (RDC; call sign Juniper) provides 24/7 EMS intake, triage support, ambulance dispatch/coordination and shared regional coverage picture under approved protocols; jurisdictions retain resource ownership/local policy. RDC records caller reports/clarifications, incidents, priorities/rationales, unit availability/assignments/status/location/time-stamped movement, zone coverage, maintenance/access constraints, authorizations/unit-selection reasons, approved alternative routes, destination changes and consultation outcomes; compares conditions to thresholds, projected response times to remaining coverage, and route/destination changes to critical-area coverage. Response zones reflect distance/roads/capacity and are reviewed after road/population/agreement changes. Computer Aided Dispatch Console (CAD Console) checks locations and presents incident/priority/travel/availability/access/staging options. Ambulance Coordination Platform consolidates unit position/status, retains time-stamped status changes, presents matching units, approved destination and operational instructions. Radio Coordinator Mistral manages Regional Radio Network/talkgroups, transmits incident identifier, location, priority, assignment, hazards, route changes; requires crew repeat-back, retries/alerts on no ack; sends Coverage Gap Bulletin. Controlled handoff only after crew ack and dispatch-floor confirmation. Paramedic Crew reports statuses, route conflicts, hazards/closures/delays, position at staging; remains staged until confirmed. Ambulance Unit 417 follows active instructions/asks clarification. Fleet Maintenance Cell Bluejay provides unavailable/restricted vehicle info and Battery Swap Voucher; RDC uses voucher to confirm battery readiness before service. North Gate Status Board displays latest queue condition/access restriction; RDC uses Queue Snapshot for northern congestion routing. South Gate Status Board displays southern access. Hospital Liaison Desk Kestrel provides facility capacity/contact/constraints, coordinates destination consultation with Emergency Department (ED), records outcome, communicates restrictions, produces Bedside Arrival Receipt. ED advises capacity/access/receiving-status changes. Shift Commander Sundial approves exceptions/nonstandard/over-capacity/staging moves and sends Mutual Aid Release Form when neighboring service released. Triage Supervisor advises demand-driven repositioning. Regional Medical Director establishes clinical priorities and guides specialized/protocol destination selection. Dispatchers consider clinical priorities/demand, response time, coverage and facility acceptance. Data Quality Officer reviews inconsistent location/status and routes corrections. RDC uses Correction Slip to reconcile destination change. Larkspur (unexpanded call sign) confirms incident identifier/intended receiving facility before destination request transmission.

New part:
S159: The Radio Coordinator relays destination instructions to the Paramedic Crew over the Regional Radio Network.
S160: The Paramedic Crew acknowledges the destination and advises dispatch if conditions require renewed consultation.
S161: The South Gate Status Board produces the South Access Lane Notice when the south approach has a material access constraint.
S162: The South Gate Status Board displays current access information for crews approaching the receiving facility through the south entrance.
S163: The Shift Commander reviews access constraints that could affect arrival timing or safe patient transfer.
S164: The Regional Radio Network supports updates between dispatch and the Paramedic Crew while the ambulance is en route.
S165: Call Taker Mara receives the Bedside Arrival Receipt to support completion of the incident record.
S166: Call Taker Mara verifies that the recorded arrival time is consistent with the dispatch timeline and crew communications.
S167: Ambulance Unit 417 reports arrival at the receiving facility and confirms when patient handover is complete.
S168: The Emergency Department and the Paramedic Crew clarify any discrepancy in patient identity or transfer documentation before the crew clears the facility.
S169: The Data Quality Officer reviews incomplete arrival or handover fields during routine record-quality checks.
S170: The Regional Dispatch Center updates the incident status after receiving confirmation that the patient has been transferred to facility care.
S171: The Hospital Liaison Desk remains available to resolve facility-level questions that arise during or immediately after handover.
S172: The Shift Commander escalates unresolved destination or access issues through established regional coordination procedures.
S173: Surge operations begin when queue age, simultaneous high-priority calls, or staffed unit availability crosses thresholds approved by regional policy.
S174: Regional Dispatch Center monitors these indicators continuously and declares the applicable surge level when a threshold is met.
S175: Computer Aided Dispatch Console displays the current surge level and the operational constraints reported by field and facility staff.
S176: Triage Supervisor validates the declaration and confirms that call prioritization remains consistent with clinical protocols.
S177: Shift Commander assigns coordination responsibilities and reviews whether normal coverage can be maintained during the surge.
S178: Regional Medical Director provides clinical direction when demand exceeds routine triage guidance or requires a regional protocol adjustment.
S179: Hospital Liaison Desk uses the Pediatric Acuity Note to convey pediatric monitoring and destination considerations to receiving staff.
S180: Pediatric calls with concerning airway, breathing, circulation, or mental status findings receive prompt clinical escalation under approved protocols.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
